alpha_tree — SEGMENTATION graph op

• Data kinds: image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.alpha_tree(image, alphas: 'Sequence[float]' = (0.0,), *, connectivity: 'int' = 4) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import seggraph; seggraph.alpha_tree(image, alphas: 'Sequence[float]' = (0.0,), *, connectivity: 'int' = 4) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("alpha_tree"))

Usage

α-tree: builds the minimum spanning tree of the grid weighted by neighbour differences (Kruskal in scipy) and returns the partition for each α using only the tree edges of weight ≤ α (alpha_tree).

scipy reads edges of weight 0 as "no edge", so only edges of weight 0 are replaced by "half the smallest positive weight" before building the tree (the edge order does not change = the minimum spanning tree is the same). Adding 1 to all edges is not used: when a difference of 0.3 is split in floating point into 0.29999999999999993 and 0.30000000000000004, rounding after +1 made the 2 equal, the tree picked the heavier one and the cut at α = 0.3 shifted (measured, test test_quasi_flat_zones_equal_mst_cut). The tree's edge weights are recomputed as |f_p − f_q| from the indices.

Returns: labels ((A, H, W) stacking the (H, W) for each α), n_zones, mst_i / mst_j / mst_w, merge_levels (tree edge weights in ascending order = merge heights), nested (whether nested in ascending order of α).
